title: Removal of Tractor Engine Systems Component and Parts

lessons.title: Removing parts from the cooling, air and fuel systems
lessons.html:
Engine systems

The engine has several systems around it: cooling (radiator, water pump, hoses, thermostat, fan), air (air filter, turbo, intercooler, intake and exhaust manifolds), fuel (tank, filters, lift pump, injection pump or rail, injectors and pipes) and lubrication (sump, oil pump, oil cooler, filter). In the workplace you help remove these parts for repair or replacement.

Make it safe

  • Engine cold. Coolant, exhaust and turbo parts get very hot.
  • Tractor on level ground, implements down, wheels chocked, key out.
  • Battery negative lead disconnected.

Cooling system parts

  1. Open the radiator cap only when the engine is cold.
  2. Drain coolant into a clean container. Coolant is poisonous to people and animals; do not leave it where dogs or livestock can drink it.
  3. Loosen hose clamps and twist hoses gently off.
  4. Remove the fan guard and fan if needed.
  5. Lift the radiator out carefully so the fins do not get damaged.

Air system parts

Remove the air filter housing and intake hoses. Cap the turbo inlet and engine intake at once with clean caps or tape. Never leave the intake open; a dropped nut or rag inside can destroy the engine.

Fuel system parts

  • No smoking, flames or welding nearby.
  • Clean around fuel fittings before opening them.
  • Put a drip tray under fittings and catch the diesel.
  • Cap every fuel pipe and port at once. Even tiny dirt can damage injectors.
  • On common rail engines, wait the time in the manual after shutdown before opening high-pressure pipes, and never open them with the engine running.

lessons.title: Removing engine parts and keeping order
lessons.html:
Removing parts from the engine itself

The mechanic may ask you to help remove the rocker cover, injectors, cylinder head, sump or other parts. Follow the mechanic and the workshop manual.

Rocker cover and injectors

  • Clean around the cover before removing it so dirt does not fall in.
  • Label injector pipes and injectors by cylinder number, for example 1 to 4 from the front.
  • Use the correct puller for stuck injectors. Do not lever them out.
  • Cap injector holes at once.

Cylinder head

The head is heavy. The mechanic loosens the head bolts in the order in the manual. You help lift the head straight up with a hoist, and put it on wooden blocks on a bench, not flat on its face, to protect the valves and injector tips. Keep pushrods and rockers in order in a labelled rack.

Sump

Drain the oil first. Support the sump while removing the last bolts. Look at the oil and the bottom of the sump for metal pieces or sludge and tell the mechanic.

Turbo

Remove the oil feed and return pipes and cap them. Cap the turbo openings. Keep the turbo upright. Do not spin the turbine with your fingers inside.

Keeping order

  1. Use trays or bags for each part with its bolts.
  2. Label everything.
  3. Photograph each step.
  4. Cover the open engine with clean plastic sheeting when you stop work.

Waste

Put used oil, coolant and diesel in separate marked containers for recycling. Never pour them on the ground or into drains; on a farm this can poison borehole water and soil.

Record

List all removed parts on the job card. Note anything unusual you saw.

Key points

  • Work on a cold engine with the battery disconnected.
  • Keep coolant away from people, dogs and livestock.
  • Cap air intakes and fuel openings at once.
  • Never open high-pressure fuel pipes with the engine running.
  • Label parts by cylinder and keep them in order.
